summary: Show chain identity and keep startup observation open after the node joins
details: Both lifecycle status and progress expose the configured network name, chain ID, genesis, P2P network ID, Bitcoin source and node role, including before chain RPC is available.

Interactive up uses the same persistent observer as status --watch and remains open after readiness or controller exit until Ctrl+C. Use up --no-watch for one-shot interactive submission; JSON and non-interactive calls remain one-shot.

Healthy services waiting for configured peers to connect or synchronize complete startup successfully without claiming overall readiness. Missing seeds, unavailable observations and service failures retain their recovery requirements.

The progress header uses controller diagnostics, distinguishes a historical manual exit followed by READY from a real failure, and preserves raw systemd state and exit status. Standard installations are recognized even when systemd PATH omits the user's local bin directory.
operator_actions: After installing the updated node tools, reopen status --watch to see the new identity and controller diagnostics. No data rebuild or chain restart is needed solely to correct the old display.
Use up --no-watch when an interactive startup command should return without attaching the persistent progress view.
